implementationSteps: REPLACE the `export {};` stub in src/ledger.ts with the full zero-import module. DEFINE + EXPORT local types `FileLedger` {readFiles, modifiedFiles, bashSideEffects: string[]} and `MessageLike` {role?:string; content?:string|ContentBlock[]; [k:string]:unknown}; DEFINE module-private `ToolCallContent` {type:"toolCall"; id; name; arguments} and `ContentBlock`. (Full content in Context > Implementation Blueprint > Data models.)

DEFINE module-private const Sets: READ_TOOL_NAMES = new Set(["read","grep","rg","glob","find","ls"]) (find+ls added — Pi's actual read-only discovery tools; no glob/rg tool in Pi); WRITE_TOOL_NAMES = new Set(["write","edit"]); BASH_TOOL_NAMES = new Set(["bash"]).

DEFINE module-private bash classification constants: READ_ONLY_BASH_COMMANDS (whitelist: ls,cat,head,tail,grep,wc,echo,find,diff,test,… EXCLUDING cd/export/source/.); FILE_MUTATING_COMMANDS = new Set([rm,rmdir,mv,cp,mkdir,touch,chmod,chown,chgrp,ln,tee,truncate,install,patch,sed,split,csplit,curl,wget] — NOT git/node/npm/make); IGNORE_PATHS = new Set([/dev/null,/dev/stdout,/dev/stderr,/dev/tty,/dev/full,/dev/zero]); REDIRECT_WRITE_RE = /(?:\d?&?>{1,2}\|?)\s*(?!&|=)([^\s;|&<>]+)/ (excludes 2>&1 fd-dup, >= comparison); FIND_MUTATING_RE = /(?:^|\s)-(?:delete|exec|ok|okdir|fls|fprint|fprint0)(?=\s|$|=)/.

EXPORT `function extractFileLedger(messages: MessageLike[]|null|undefined, range: number[]|null|undefined): FileLedger`: coerce inputs (Array.isArray else []), three Sets (read/modified/bash); for each index i: skip non-integer/negative/out-of-bounds; msg=list[i]; skip if not isRecord or readOwn(msg,"role")!=="assistant"; content=readOwn(msg,"content"); skip if not Array; for each block skip non-record or readOwn(block,"type")!=="toolCall"; call classifyToolCall(name,args,...). Return {readFiles:dedupeSorted(read), modifiedFiles:dedupeSorted(modified), bashSideEffects:dedupeSorted(bash)}.

ADD module-private classifyToolCall(name,args,read,modified,bash): empty name→return; READ_TOOL_NAMES→pathArg(args)→read.add; WRITE_TOOL_NAMES→pathArg(args)→modified.add; BASH_TOOL_NAMES→command=isRecord(args)?readStringField(args,"command"):""; empty or isReadOnlyBash(command)→return; else bash.add(command) (HIGH-RECALL verbatim) + for p of extractWritePaths(command): modified.add(p) (HIGH-PRECISION). Unknown name→ignore. Plus helpers pathArg (path ?? file_path), isReadOnlyBash (every top-level segment read-only, no redirect), isSegmentReadOnly (no redirect, cmd in whitelist, find-guarded), extractWritePaths (redirect targets + file-like args from FILE_MUTATING_COMMANDS), hasWriteRedirect, extractRedirectTargets (global regex loop, drop IGNORE_PATHS), looksLikeFilePath (reject URLs/ssh/flags/numbers/operators/fd-dup/./sed-programs; accept paths-with-slash/extensions/./dotfiles), splitTopLevel (quote-aware on | ; && || \n), firstCommandName (first non-env-assignment token basename), splitShellTokens (quote-aware whitespace, strips quotes).

ADD module-private defensive helpers that NEVER throw (mirror src/tokens.ts): dedupeSorted(set)=[...set].sort() (lexicographic, case-sensitive); stripQuotes(token) (one layer of surrounding quotes); readStringField(obj,key) (string or ""); isRecord(v) (object, not null, not array); readOwn(obj,key) (try/catch the get → undefined on Proxy throw). Confirm we read ONLY .path/.file_path/.command — NEVER JSON.stringify(arguments) (so circular arguments are harmless).

successCriteria.description: src/ledger.ts exports extractFileLedger(messages, range) and types FileLedger {readFiles, modifiedFiles, bashSideEffects: string[]} and MessageLike; imports NOTHING (no Pi/config/tokens/log). range is a number[] of message indices (Unit.indices from the rewind resolver), NOT a [start,end) tuple.

The spec/10 §1.6 PINNED example reproduces EXACTLY: read(a.ts)+edit(b.ts)+bash(git commit)+bash(ls) over range [0,1,2,3] → { readFiles:["a.ts"], modifiedFiles:["b.ts"], bashSideEffects:["git commit"] } (ls omitted as read-only).
Empty span (range []), empty messages, null messages, null range each → { readFiles:[], modifiedFiles:[], bashSideEffects:[] }.

readFiles = union of path ?? file_path from {read,grep,rg,glob,find,ls}; modifiedFiles = union of path ?? file_path from {write,edit} + high-confidence bash write paths; bashSideEffects = non-provably-read-only bash commands verbatim. Unknown tool names ignored (forward-compat).

The bash policy is ASYMMETRIC: bashSideEffects is HIGH-RECALL (whitelist of provably-read-only commands + write-redirect detection + find-destructive-flag detection; anything else included verbatim, 'when in doubt include'); modifiedFiles-from-bash is HIGH-PRECISION (redirect targets + file-like args from FILE_MUTATING_COMMANDS only; git/node/npm/make → bashSideEffects ONLY).

git commit → bashSideEffects ONLY (modifiedFiles empty); node/npm → modifiedFiles empty; curl -o out.txt URL extracts out.txt while curl URL extracts nothing; /dev/null,/dev/stdout,/dev/stderr,/dev/tty,/dev/full,/dev/zero never appear in modifiedFiles.

find -delete and find -exec classify as bashSideEffects (NOT read-only) despite find being in the read-only whitelist; ls 2>&1 | cat is a read-only pipeline (2>&1 is fd-duplication, not a file write).
All three lists are de-duplicated and lexicographically sorted (case-sensitive, [...set].sort()); paths are returned VERBATIM with no cwd normalization / no filesystem access.

extractFileLedger NEVER throws on adversarial input: throwing-Proxy accessors (readOwn swallows the get trap → undefined), circular arguments (only .path/.file_path/.command read, never JSON.stringify(arguments)), non-array content, non-record/non-toolCall blocks, out-of-bounds/non-integer/garbage indices — all skipped defensively to an empty or partial ledger.

test/ledger.test.ts is green and covers all 6 tiers: spec/10 §1.6 pinned contract + empty/null cases; readFiles classification; modifiedFiles classification; bashSideEffects classification (high-recall); range iteration (assistant-only, toolResult/user/out-of-bounds skipped); defensive never-throws + type-level expectTypeOf.
npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 and npx vitest run (full suite) shows no regression in the existing config/log/tokens/runtime/load tests.
